source_text:
«Ἐγὼ κρίνω»· οὗ τὴν κρίσιν ἀθετεῖν οὐ

θέμις, οὐδὲ φαυλίζειν τὸ ψήφισμα· «Ἐν ἐμοὶ γὰρ ὁ πάντων κριτὴς καὶ νεκρῶν καὶ
ζώντων φθέγγεται. Ἐμὸν τὸ ὄργανον, ἀλλ' ὁ τεχνίτης ὑπὲρ ἐμέ. Ἐγὼ τὴν γλῶσσαν
παρέχω, ἀλλ' ὁ δημιουργὸς Λόγος τὸν λόγον χορηγεῖ. Μὴ τῷ καλάμῳ, τῷ δὲ
γράφοντι πρόσεχε. Τὴν ἀκοὴν ὑπακοὴ διαδεχέσθω.»

1
orientation: Hesychius is explaining that James's words at the apostolic council are not merely human, but the voice of Christ the judge of all speaking through James as an instrument.
pass_a_gloss: "I judge": whose judgment to set aside [is] not lawful, nor to disparage the decree. "For in me the judge of all, both of dead and of living, speaks. Mine [is] the instrument, but the craftsman [is] above me. I supply the tongue, but the creator Word supplies the word. Do not attend to the reed, but to the one writing. Let obedience succeed the hearing."

choices.why: θέμις denotes what is divinely or customarily permitted; 'lawful' preserves the religious-legal force without importing modern legal terminology.
The verb means to treat as worthless or make light of; 'disparage' captures the active belittling force.
In civic Greek a ψήφισμα is a formal resolution; 'decree' keeps the official, binding character of James's judgment.
The verb suggests utterance or sounding forth; 'speaks' is plain and preserves the present-tense ongoing force.
The κάλαμος is the reed pen; 'reed' keeps the concrete image of the writing instrument, paired with the one writing.
The imperative means 'let one thing take the place of another'; 'let obedience succeed the hearing' preserves the sequence of hearing followed by obedience.

pass_b_english: “I judge.” It is not lawful to set aside his judgment, nor to despise his decree. For in me speaks the judge of all, both the dead and the living. The instrument is mine, but the craftsman is above me. I supply the tongue, but the Word, the maker, supplies the word. Pay no attention to the reed, but to the one who writes with it. Let obedience follow the hearing.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'the Word' for Λόγος; 'maker' is banned per τεχνίτης entry.
last_rejected.fix: I supply the tongue, but the Word, the craftsman, supplies the word.
last_rejected.ruling: Source has ὁ δημιουργὸς Λόγος; 'the Word, the maker' renders both terms accurately without glossary conflict.

last_rejected.quote: Pay no attention to the reed
last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'instrument' for ὄργανον; 'reed' obscures the instrument/craftsman wordplay.
last_rejected.fix: Pay no attention to the instrument
last_rejected.ruling: Source Μὴ τῷ καλάμῳ literally means 'the reed'; rendering as 'reed' is within normal range, not a glossary violation.

last_rejected.quote: It is not lawful to set aside his judgment
last_rejected.source_quote: οὗ τὴν κρίσιν ἀθετεῖν οὐ θέμις
last_rejected.why: English 'his' hides the voice shift: source uses masculine οὗ referring back to James, but the following lines show Christ speaking through James. The ambiguity should be preserved or clarified.
last_rejected.fix: It is not lawful to set aside this judgment
last_rejected.ruling: οὗ is masculine genitive 'whose/of whom'; 'his' correctly renders it. Voice-shift ambiguity is interpretive, not mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: διαδεχέσθω is imperative 'let...receive/succeed,' but 'succeed the hearing' is opaque; 'let obedience follow hearing' or 'let hearing be met with obedience' conveys the sense.
last_rejected.fix: Let hearing be met with obedience
last_rejected.ruling: διαδεχέσθω means 'succeed/follow'; 'succeed the hearing' is awkward but within word's range, not a major error.

polish.changed: Clarified that the quoted speech is James speaking as Christ's instrument, made the pronoun referents explicit, and smoothed the final metaphor for modern readers.

notes.why: Quotation marks open but speaker shifts: James? Homilist? Christ? Unclear who speaks.
notes.fix: Clarify attribution: James speaks, then homilist, then Christ through James.

notes.quote: For in me speaks the judge
notes.why: Who is 'me'? James? Homilist? Pronoun referent lost across section break.
notes.fix: Identify speaker as James or homilist assuming James's voice.

notes.why: Same problem: 'I' = James? Homilist? Reader cannot track.
notes.fix: Consistent speaker labels or stage directions.

notes.quote: For in me speaks the judge of all, both the dead and the living
notes.why: Ambiguous whether 'me' is James speaking or the homilist himself.
notes.fix: Clarify: the homilist quotes James, who says Christ speaks in him.

notes.quote: Pay no attention to the reed, but to the one writing
notes.why: Unclear who 'the one writing' is—Christ or God the Father.
notes.fix: Specify: 'to Christ, who writes through me.'
